title: I Seen a Man Die
year_note: The year is the original's. This recording is an AI-made soul cover posted on YouTube, and its upload title is all we know about it.
album: YouTube upload; the original is on The Diary

titles: Scarface – I Seen a Man Die (50s Soul Version)

notes.made: N.O. Joe, Mike Dean and Scarface produced it for Rap-A-Lot, and the album leaned on in-house studio musicians more than samples. RapReviews hears a reverberating bassline, a somber synth arrangement and sleigh bells. Scarface has said N.O. Joe brought him 'a new sound', a funky swing with heavy drums.
notes.context: It was the first single from The Diary, out September 27, 1994, ahead of the album on October 18. The song follows a man out of prison after seven years who tries to go straight, slides back into crime and dies; the later verses look back from the far side of it. For the single it was retitled 'Never Seen a Man Cry', and it became Scarface's first top 40 hit, at number 37, while the album went to number two and was platinum by December.

listen_for.where: the low end from the start
listen_for.note: the reverberating bassline and somber synths sit under everything, with sleigh bells on top, a slow bed a soul arrangement can keep.
it's one story told start to finish, the shape of a ballad more than a party record, so a slow soul arrangement fits its pace.

leads_to.title: Six Feet Deep
leads_to.why: Scarface and N.O. Joe a year earlier, a funeral song built on the Commodores' 'Easy' and Marvin Gaye's 'What's Going On'.

notes.unverified: The Diary's Wikipedia page lists a sample of Julie Driscoll, Brian Auger and the Trinity's 'Light My Fire' on this track, but the song's own page names no sample and I couldn't confirm it anywhere else, so I left it out. No video director found.

culture.title: First top 40
culture.line: Number 37 on the Hot 100, number 15 R&B and number two on Hot Rap Songs, one of only two Hot 100 entries in Scarface's career.
